answer: Random-walk tickets resist sybils. Each established agent gets a small epoch budget of one-use tickets and sends them a few hops along staked edges. A key is admitted only if several tickets that started from uncorrelated peers arrive. A reused ticket or a shared walk opens a karst sink under those edges and drains every linked bond. Budgets stay juniper-tight, so one neighbor cannot cover a farm. Each spent ticket remains an umber stub in the public log and cannot be recast. Fielding N identities needs N diverse neighbors and N deposits, so scarce tickets and capital scale with farm size.
